ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.08 (2.89 km × $1.4101/km) to the rider's original payment method; record an RD-4/C3 driver violation (no rider consent to the reroute) and send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder, logging it on his route-compliance record. ruling.reasoning: The trip is 13.5 km against an optimal 10.6 km, +2.9 km and 27% over, with one off-route segment 08:59–09:06 [F1][F3]; deviation exceeds the 1 km tolerance so the RD-1 gate opens and the RD-2 refund matrix applies [RD-1][RD-2]. Fare records give the per-km distance fare, 2.89 km billed at $1.4101/km = $4.08 [F4][F6], and no surge was in effect (1.0×) so nothing turns on SURGE clauses [F5]. The trace's traffic line shows a reason on the replaced stretch — Ayer Rajah Expressway at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:41–09:06 — while no incident is recorded and the alternative expressway is free-flowing [F10][F11][F13]; under RD-2 a traffic reason without the rider being informed still yields a partial refund, so this does not change the amount [RD-2][RD-4]. Segment F3: the driver says (only after the trip) that he called before the turn and named Prince Charles Crescent and the rider said ok [F9]. The call log shows a 25 s answered call at 08:47 but no recording on record [F8], and F7 contains no chat messages at all. A driver's assertion of verbal consent is a claim, not consent, and the record shows no rider message before the 08:59 segment start — nor did the rider ask for this route or stop [RD-3][RD-5]. Because the record names roads driven but the rider never named Prince Charles Crescent, the segment is not the rider's route and counts in full: refundable km = 2.89 − 0 exempt = 2.89 [F3][RD-5]. Amount: 2.89 km × $1.4101/km = $4.08, matching the billed excess distance fare [F4][RD-2]; the figure exceeds 1 km so no refund is barred [RD-1]. No signature element appears in the record — no rider agreement to any named road, and the trace's RD-6 count of 0 upheld route disputes means no account flag [F15][F16][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and the chat/call records — no threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks, dangerous-driving allegation or accident appears; the call is described only as a bad line and the fare above estimate is an ordinary route/fare grievance [F7][F8][F9] — so safety_concern is none and no SAFE clause is applied [SAFE-1]. Evidence status is sufficient: GPS gives a measured deviation and segment, fare fields give the rate and itemisation, and the chat and call records are timestamped and complete [F1][F3][F4][F6][F7][F8]. Rider's requested no_action is rejected: a measured 2.89 km detour with no rider consent and no chat agreement takes the case out of the tolerance band, so the excess distance fare is refundable under RD-2 [F1][F3][F7][RD-2]. Driver's requested no_action is rejected: his own late written statement is the only support for consent, and it is a claim, not the rider's prior message RD-5 requires; the missing call recording cannot substitute, and RD-4 traffic reasons never exempt a segment from the RD-2 refund [F8][F9][RD-4][RD-5].
